prospect.name: Alex Shivelhood
prospect.occupation: Licensed insurance agent selling Medicare health plans to seniors; describes it as a new career after a period of homelessness roughly seven years ago
prospect.family_status: Lives with his male partner and family in a recently bought house, having gone from living alone to a household of four; his partner has an elderly mother he helps care for. Was previously married to a Dutch man who died; also lost his mother, father and brother within the same three-year period while acting as their caregiver.
prospect.training_background: Has been in and out of gyms since age 13 and enjoys them, but says he never really knew what to do. Two and a half years ago hired a personal trainer and lost 70 lb through nutrition, walking and intermittent fasting with no resistance training and insufficient protein. Currently not training at all; walks about 7,000 steps a day and has hit a plateau. Tracking macros loosely with free apps at roughly 125-150 g protein, 70-80 g carbs and 1,700-2,000 calories a day.
prospect.medical: Bicycle accident roughly eighteen months ago: eleven broken ribs on one side, a broken clavicle and a punctured lung, with about six months of recovery. A nerve block given for rib pain damaged the nerve supplying an abdominal wall muscle on his right side, which is now denervated and visibly protruding; a plastic surgeon told him it may never recover and that the nerve might regenerate over a couple of years. He states he has since been cleared by two doctors with no restrictions on exercise. Went into a significant depression after the accident and regained 50 of the 70 lb lost. History of drug use and homelessness roughly seven years ago, now resolved; describes emotional eating as a lifelong pattern and says he does not believe he needs therapy for it. At 230 lb and 5'7" he describes visceral body fat as his central health concern and fears heart attack, stroke and cancer.

signals: Lost ground to a specific, identifiable event: 'I had a bicycle accident, broke 11 ribs and clavicle and punctured my lung, went into bad depression afterwards. And I gained 50 back.'
Explicitly wants a former self back and has the number: from 230 lb to the 185 he reached two and a half years ago
Visible regret and exhaustion at starting over: 'when you get older, it's almost like you get exhausted having to start over again. So I was faced yet again. Okay, I got start over again.'
Frames it as recovery rather than optimisation: 'I have to save my life. Because that's what I'm doing here, saving my life.'

Get back to 185 lb from 230 lb, and possibly lower depending on muscle composition
Build actual muscle this time, which he skipped entirely during the previous 70 lb loss
Improve mobility and stiffness - 'cricking and popping' and not bending as well since 45

Make it sustainable and repeatable for the rest of his life rather than another yo-yo cycle
Put his own oxygen mask on first after a lifetime of caring for others, and then inspire others with the story
Something simple and streamlined he can take travelling and use in any gym
